approved_findings: Old line 45 required L0 KYC submission before collecting payment methods. New lines 38 and 50 explicitly permit Apple Pay or Google Pay collection before Link authentication/KYC for iOS, Android, and React Native, using wallet name/address to prefill L0. New line 50 retains a separate gate: registration or authentication plus minimum identity information before createCryptoPaymentToken. Collection is not verification, token creation, session creation, purchase, or payment success. Current source line 23 and concept line 105 need qualification.

The new guide separates Link registration contact data from KYC API input: wallet email/phone are for Link, while firstName, lastName and address go to attachKYCInfo/attachKycInfo (new line 38). Current source's L0 input table at line 19 is a tier-level requirement, not a single attachKYCInfo body schema; preserve that distinction.

Old line 128 interpreted crypto_onramp_missing_minimum_identity_verification as L0 verification failed. New lines 50 and 131 interpret it as missing minimum identity submission. A customer who submitted minimum data but failed L0 may pass L1, which supersedes L0 (new lines 52 and 131). Current source line 37 must change; do not treat an L0 rejection as automatic permanent ineligibility.

New line 11 adds EU identifier/attestation requirements beyond standard tiers, and new line 141 adds a risk-rule identity challenge as a possible cause of L2/document verification even below the current tier's transaction limit. Both are material qualifications missing from the old capture/source.

The tier table, asynchronous L0/L1 verification, 400 on pending verification before session creation, five status values, highest attempted tier definition, deprecated verifications fallback, and partial L1/L2 step-up paths remain substantively stable (old lines 18-41, 49-112, 114-142; new lines 21-46, 56-115, 117-144). Current tier includes pending/rejected and does not by itself mean verified.
approved_conflicts: The new error table says prompt the customer to submit name, phone, email and address 'using attachKYCInfo' at line 131, while new line 38 explicitly says email and phone are used for Link registration and are not submitted through the KYC API. Preserve the split: Link contact registration plus KYC name/address submission; do not infer attachKYCInfo accepts phone/email.

The existing source line 23 and concept line 105 claim L0 before collectPaymentMethod, conflicting with new Platform Pay collection before registration/authentication/KYC at lines 38 and 50. Restrict the correction to the newly described mobile Platform Pay path; other payment methods are not authorized for pre-auth collection by this guide.

The existing concept wiki/concepts/stripe-crypto-onramp.md line 93 and related May 2026 source wiki/sources/source-stripe-crypto-onramp-embedded-components-integration.md line 17 state Embedded Components headless mode is US only, excluding New York. The November same-URL KYC guide at new line 11 addresses EU customers' additional identifier and attestation requirements. This creates a dated regional-scope tension requiring concept qualification and verification against the linked EU KYC guide; it does not establish EU merchant eligibility or remove the older restriction.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the old guide's L0-before-payment-method statement as dated May 2026 guidance, not a current universal prerequisite in the November mobile Platform Pay flow (old line 45; new lines 38, 50).
All customers must pass sufficient KYC before buying crypto; Platform Pay collection does not confer verification or payment completion (new lines 9, 50).
